checks: Source fc542fd7a6ea864e §§1–3 (1)–(2) gives the same one-sided dual, tuple estimate and endpoint-budget aggregation. The frozen result assumes the couplings and convex order and does not assert their geometric existence.

Maximizing the concave dual expression over t≥0 yields the stated two scalar branches, including q=0. Compactness bounds the optimizer. The truncated supremum of globally convex physical tests with nonnegative t and affine A_i gives the extension of F_q, and max_i(q−A_i)_+ gives the weight extension.

At a midpoint, Jensen gives the lower bound at averaged (q,L), and monotonicity in q permits replacing the averaged q by q(b). If q(b)>L(b), the branch difference is q(b) log(1/a)−L(b)(1−a), at least (q(b)−L(b)) log(1/a). The zero-weight case follows from convexity.

Weighted Jensen with weights w_q(b)dπ/T uses only the set of positive weight, whose gap integral is at most Δ. Convex order for F_q bounds Δ by the old gap, and midpoint Jensen for w_q bounds T by T_end. The perspective is increasing in both budgets and bounded by dΔ.

The endpoint-zero convention is justified by the bound B_d(T,Δ)≤T. Concavity and degree-one homogeneity give the sum or integral over supplied components, including zero-T components. Source domination increases the entropy budget by convex order. All q use the original fixed π.

overlap.comparison: Provides actual same-normal couplings with conditional convex-order improvement and a parity-dependent surface capacity under its geometric hypotheses. This theorem assumes couplings and estimates their discounted error, with no parity factor in that error budget.
Provides a specific three-fiber midpoint repair and halfspace cost with fixed crossflows. It does not prove the one-sided entropy tuple bound or the nonlinear convex-weight error budget.

readability: The number-of-components statement concerns only aggregation of already supplied entropy budgets. It makes no assertion about a separate baseline capacity cost.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The one-sided entropy correction gives globally convex tests for convex weights and bounds the discounted error for the supplied couplings. The nonlinear bound aggregates without a factor from the number of components.
